title: Watching the Seven Samurai 4K Restoration in a packed cinema was one of the most magical experiences of my life.

commenti.body: Didn't see the 4k restoration, but I did see it around a year ago at the BFI imax in London, which was probably just as good. Seeing it with an audience makes you realise how funny some of Kurosawa's films are. He always strikes a perfect blend between drama and comedy.
Yep I was surprised by how funny Seven Samurai was, great chemistry between the ensemble and cracking dialogue

That 4k is "S tier" quality and is jaw dropping considering its 70 years old. it really is one of those "oh you don't think 4K adds anything? Well look at this!". As for the film. It just completely rocks and I love how vicious the violence is, it's like there's very little glorifying it. At 200+min, it never wastes a moment. It's up there in the best films ever made. Period.

Just saw it on the weekend in Melbourne Australia at the Astor. And yeah it was a transcendant experience. The audience at the end actually applauded which they very rarely do here. The picture is simply exquisite, I've seen it in a theatre before and this is the best its looked for me. I can easily believe its the best its looked bar new original prints.

Yes! My husband and I saw the 4k restoration at our city's fine arts museum. It was sold out and a wonderful experience to see it with so many others on a large screen. Tons of laughs throughout. I had seen the first half before, but it was my first time to see the entire thing, and the lingering feelings it left were a complete shock to me, honestly. Wonderful experience. 




Film is not an art form I was naturally drawn to. I respected it, but did not study it at all. My husband dove deeply into film a few years ago and has pulled me along with him. I'm so very glad he did.

I saw it at Film Forum in NYC during its run there, and I agree it was magical, not only to see the film in a crisp and clean restoration, but also to see a packed theater with such a variety of people watching: films buffs and film snobs, sure, but also couples on a date, twenty-somethings initially daunted by the idea of sitting through a 3.5-hour movie, and folks curious to see what all the fuss is about. The movie flew by, everyone seemed captivated, and there was such a positive chatter from people as we all exited the theater. Seven Samurai is foundational filmmaking, for sure, but it's also an excellent theater-going experience.

The one disadvantage of rural living is the nearest theater that plays these types of showings is hours away in Pittsburgh. Our more local theaters will literally show the latest Ghostbusters movie every day for months, I guess cause the licensing is cheaper than actual good films. It sucks.

Ideally you'd see every movie on the big screen in good quality but this is one of those that really adds to the experience. I waited years to see Lawrence of Arabia on the big screen as I knew it would be best in that way and I wish I did the same for Seven Samurai!
